Denver International Airport and downtown development interests opposed. Council vote: 11-2 in favor (only two pro-development votes). moratoriums.summary: The nation's first statewide data center moratorium. Executive Order No. 62, signed July 14, 2026, directs the Department of Environmental Conservation to hold in abeyance all pending applications for any discretionary permit, approval or license for constructing or expanding a data center of 50 MW or more (applications deemed complete before the order are excluded). It suspends state environmental permitting only — local government permits are not covered. The pause runs until the Department of Public Service delivers a final Generic Environmental Impact Statement assessing energy demand, water use and quality, air quality, disproportionate community impacts and noise; press reporting describes it as up to a year. Facilities primarily used for manufacturing, research (including quantum computing), accredited education (including the Empire AI consortium) or medical care are exempt. Empire State Development must post a 'Community Investment Framework' within 60 days covering community investment funds, local infrastructure, labor frameworks and transparency reporting. The order is a separate instrument from the one-year moratorium bill (S10642/A11560) passed by the legislature, which Hochul has not signed. Note: the governor's office describes this as the nation's first statewide moratorium on hyperscale data centers, but this dataset already tracks several earlier-enacted state moratoriums (e.g. Oklahoma 2024, Washington 2024, Hawaii Jan 2026, Vermont Mar 2026, Maine and Massachusetts Apr 2026, Florida May 2026) — the 'first' framing appears to be a self-characterization, not independently verified here.

moratoriums.duration_description: Indefinite administrative pause pending a comprehensive ERCOT/PUCT audit; ERCOT anticipates the audit will take several months, but no fixed end date has been announced.
moratoriums.summary: This is a governor's administrative directive, not a legislative moratorium — recorded separately per this dataset's convention of not force-fitting an executive action into the 'bill' shape (same treatment as ny-state-eo62-2026-07). On August 3, 2026, Governor Greg Abbott directed the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT) and ERCOT to conduct a 'comprehensive verification and audit' of data center projects in ERCOT's interconnection queue — covering power use/generation, water consumption and cooling, community-impact mitigation, facility ownership, and tax incentives — before any additional projects may proceed; Abbott said any project failing to comply 'must be denied connection to the Texas grid.' The queue holds roughly 474 GW of pending interconnection requests (over 5x ERCOT's peak demand), about 90% of it data centers; ERCOT immediately paused its 'Batch Zero' interconnection study process the same day. On September 14, 2026 Abbott issued a second, related directive to the Texas Water Development Board (TWDB), ordering it to compel major water users including data centers to complete legally required water-use surveys and to penalize those that don't: noncompliant users can face a Class C misdemeanor and become ineligible for TCEQ permits, permit amendments or renewals, with the Governor's office citing roughly 28% survey response compliance over the last three years; TWDB must report back to the Governor's office on enforcement progress by October 14, 2026. The directive took effect immediately and is already blocking new interconnections, so it is tracked as 'enacted' per schema.py's status contract (enacted = in effect as of capture date; permanence is a separate axis from whether it is currently in force) — this is a pause pending audit, not a permanent ban, and no project has been permanently barred, but the pause itself is live, not merely proposed.

On September 1, 2026 the commissioners extended the moratorium for another 180 days, with County Administrator Chas Cannon pointing to Floyd County's water-related restrictions as a model for the county's eventual ordinance.
moratoriums.source_title: Moultrie Observer — Commission adopts a moratorium on data centers (June 8, 2026)

resources.title: Moultrie Observer — County extends data center moratorium (Sept 8, 2026)

moratoriums.policy_type: County commission moratorium on data center construction, pending zoning-ordinance revisions

moratoriums.duration_description: 12 months from July 28, 2026
moratoriums.summary: The Albany City Commission on Tuesday, July 28, 2026 unanimously approved a 12-month moratorium pausing new data center developments in the city, giving city leaders time to establish regulations before any new projects can proceed. Separate from the Dougherty County record (dougherty-county-ga-2026-07): the county's review period covers unincorporated Dougherty County, of which Albany is the seat.
moratoriums.source_title: WALB — Data center developments paused for 12 months in Albany following commission vote (July 29, 2026)
moratoriums.policy_type: City commission moratorium on new data center developments

moratoriums.duration_description: 12 months from August 31, 2026
moratoriums.summary: Mead's Board of Trustees approved a 12-month moratorium on data centers at its August 31, 2026 meeting, with six of the seven trustees present; the 4-2 vote (Trustees Brad Hagan and Jeremiah Crane opposed) adopted a moratorium that prevents data centers from applying to develop within the town. Reported by a single outlet, the Berthoud Weekly Surveyor.
moratoriums.source_title: Berthoud Weekly Surveyor — Mead trustees approve 12-month data center moratorium
moratoriums.policy_type: Town Board of Trustees moratorium on data center applications
moratoriums.city_council_vote: 4-2 (Trustees Brad Hagan and Jeremiah Crane opposed; six of seven trustees present), August 31, 2026

moratoriums.duration_description: 6 months (through approximately November 26, 2026); applies only to facilities designed with a capacity greater than 5 megawatts. Not an extension yet as of this capture, but the Planning Commission has scheduled two public hearings (Oct. 16 and Nov. 16, 2026) toward a longer-term data-center ordinance, per Mayor Dan Brady.
moratoriums.summary: The Bloomington City Council voted (Mollie Ward dissenting) on May 26, 2026 to approve a 6-month moratorium on data center development, specifically for facilities over 5 MW capacity, while the city studies regulations. This is a separate action from neighboring Normal's moratorium, which has no MW threshold.
moratoriums.source_title: WGLT — Bloomington approves 6-month moratorium on data centers

resources.title: 25News Now — Normal to consider longer moratorium on data centers, Bloomington schedules 2 public hearings (Sept. 20, 2026)

moratoriums.duration_description: Extended September 21, 2026 by another six months, through May 31, 2027. Applies to all data centers, with no megawatt threshold.
moratoriums.summary: The Town of Normal's council approved a moratorium on new data centers on Monday, May 18, 2026, to give officials time to study how to regulate the facilities, with no minimum-capacity threshold (unlike neighboring Bloomington's pause, which covers only facilities over 5 MW). On Monday, September 21, 2026, the council extended it another six months, through May 31, 2027; Andy Byars was the only council member to vote against.
moratoriums.source_title: WGLT — Normal Town Council hears financial trends, approves data center moratorium extension (Sept. 22, 2026)

resources.title: 25News Now — Data center pause approved in Normal, Bloomington likely to follow (May 18-19, 2026)
WGLT — Normal proposes 6-month extension to data center moratorium (Sept. 18, 2026)
The Pantagraph — Normal council OKs data center moratorium to develop regulations (May 19, 2026)

moratoriums.city_council_vote: Sept 21 extension: Andy Byars the only vote against

moratoriums.duration_description: 12 months (proposed); Ordinance 26-42 requires two public hearings. The Planning Commission reviewed the draft Sept. 17, 2026; the Board of County Commissioners held the first public hearing Sept. 22, 2026, and advanced it; the second and final public hearing / adoption vote is scheduled for Oct. 6, 2026.
moratoriums.summary: Manatee County commissioners on September 22, 2026 advanced, at the first of two required public hearings, Ordinance 26-42, which would impose a 12-month moratorium on applications for building permits, site plans, development orders, rezonings and comprehensive plan amendments for data centers and other large-load customers in unincorporated Manatee County. The second and final public hearing is scheduled for October 6, 2026. The county acted under authority granted by Florida's newly effective SB 484. Commissioner Amanda Ballard said the pause will let staff address gaps in county regulations, since neither the land development code nor the comprehensive plan currently address large-load customers.
moratoriums.source_title: Your Observer / East County News — Manatee County issues one-year ban on data centers

resources.title: Pulse of Manatee — Manatee Commissioners to Consider Data Center Moratorium, Gambling Regulations and Land Conservation

moratoriums.duration_description: Up to 1 year (interim ordinance); takes effect upon adoption and publication and can end earlier if the city repeals it or adopts replacement regulations first.
moratoriums.summary: The Woodbury City Council voted on September 23, 2026 to approve a moratorium on new data centers and on expansion beyond existing approvals, giving the city up to a year to study water use, electricity demand, noise and possible zoning changes. The ordinance blocks related rezoning proposals, comprehensive plan amendments, conditional use permits, variances and permit applications (including building, electrical and right-of-way permits) to establish or expand data centers, and also covers proposed water or sewer users whose annual consumption would place them among the city's largest users. Woodbury has three existing data centers, including two IronGate facilities and a Medtronic facility.
moratoriums.source_title: Woodbury News Net — Woodbury Approves Data Center Moratorium After Questions About Water, Power

resources.title: Woodbury News Net — Woodbury Proposes Data Center Moratorium Ahead Of Sept. 23 Council Meeting

moratoriums.duration_description: 90 days, to give the city time to draft zoning changes (define data centers, set residential buffers and accountability requirements, form a community advisory committee).
moratoriums.summary: In a special called meeting on August 31, 2026, the Forest Park City Council approved a 90-day data center moratorium to give the city time to revise its zoning laws. Under current zoning, data centers are allowed by right, which already let Digital Realty build a facility in Forest Park. City Manager Carl Geffken said the goal is not to stop data centers but to set buffers, definitions and accountability provisions.
moratoriums.source_title: News-Daily — Forest Park Council passes 90-day data center moratorium

moratoriums.duration_description: 6 months from Aug. 3, 2026. The town council, planning and zoning board and water board will hold public informational sessions while the town studies potential economic and infrastructure impacts.
moratoriums.summary: The Harpersville town council approved a 6-month data center moratorium at its August 3, 2026 meeting to allow time to study the potential economic and infrastructure impacts data centers could have on the town, with the planning and zoning board and water board hosting a series of public informational sessions.
moratoriums.source_title: WBRC — Harpersville town council approves 6-month data center moratorium

moratoriums.duration_description: 45 days (interim urgency ordinance); staff plans to return by Oct. 10, 2026 with findings, and the council could extend it by 10 months and 15 days and then up to another year if needed.
moratoriums.summary: The Escondido City Council unanimously approved a 45-day moratorium on August 26, 2026, at staff's recommendation, prohibiting new data centers and expansion or intensification of existing facilities while the city studies water and electricity demand, grid strain, large footprints and cooling-system/generator noise. The city had no pending data center applications at the time.
moratoriums.source_title: The Coast News — Escondido temporarily bans new AI data centers

moratoriums.duration_description: 1 year, unanimously approved by the Board of Commissioners Tuesday night, Sept. 1, 2026, citing a lack of specific zoning rules for data centers.
moratoriums.summary: The Winchester Board of Commissioners voted unanimously on September 1, 2026 to enact a one-year moratorium on data center development, following a staff presentation outlining similar pauses already in place across central and eastern Kentucky, to give the city time to study impacts on utilities, rates and the environment and gather community input.
moratoriums.source_title: Winchester Sun — Winchester enacts one-year data center moratorium amid regional wave of restrictions

moratoriums.duration_description: 12 months, given emergency reading and passed 4-0 Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026 (one councilman absent). Council simultaneously repealed a since-unused 2024 moratorium on marijuana dispensary permits.
moratoriums.summary: Newton Falls Village Council voted 4-0 on September 2, 2026 to give emergency reading to a 12-month moratorium on data center permits, so the zoning department and city manager can research infrastructure, utilities and zoning-code implications before any proposal arrives. One councilman called instead for a permanent ban, citing no local land suited to large facilities.
moratoriums.source_title: Tribune Chronicle (tribtoday.com) — Newton Falls enacts 1-year moratorium on data centers

resources.title: WFMJ — Newton Falls imposes yearlong moratorium on data centers

moratoriums.duration_description: 1 year, voted unanimously after a public hearing on Wednesday night, Aug. 12, 2026, to give the Board of Trustees time to review public health, land use, environmental and general welfare impacts before enacting a permanent ordinance.
moratoriums.summary: The Village of Bellevue's board voted unanimously (5-0) on August 12, 2026 to enact a one-year moratorium on data center development after a public hearing where residents raised concerns about environmental degradation, noise pollution, fossil-fuel pollution, water supply and electric bills. Bellevue joins other Wisconsin communities including Greenleaf, Manitowoc County, Dane County, Caledonia, Superior and Cassville.
moratoriums.source_title: NBC 26 — Village of Bellevue bans data center development for 12 months

moratoriums.duration_description: 3 years, approved Aug. 17, 2026, remaining in place through August 31, 2029 -- the second-longest pause in Arkansas after Independence County's. Applies to data centers, digital asset mining businesses and other large-scale computer/server operations.
moratoriums.summary: The Madison County Quorum Court approved a three-year moratorium on data centers, digital-asset-mining businesses and other large-scale computer/server operations on August 17, 2026, remaining in effect through August 31, 2029, to give county officials time to study the potential costs and benefits and develop regulations. Madison County has no known data center project in development; it is the fifth Arkansas county to adopt a three-year pause.
moratoriums.source_title: KATV — Madison County Quorum Court approves three-year moratorium on data centers

moratoriums.duration_description: 6 months, unanimously approved at the city council meeting Tuesday night, Aug. 18, 2026, after residents raised concerns about a roughly 450-acre proposed site along Highway 280 and Cheshire Drive.
moratoriums.summary: Westover city leaders unanimously voted at their August 18, 2026 council meeting to implement a six-month moratorium on data centers after neighbors raised concerns about the land, environmental and other costs of a proposed roughly 450-acre data center site. Mayor Bobby Pardue said the pause gives the city time to research data centers, zoning, and the project's potential community impacts.
moratoriums.source_title: WBRC — Westover approves 6-month moratorium on data centers

resources.title: ABC 3340 — Westover City Council unanimously approves 6-month moratorium on data centers

moratoriums.jurisdiction: Garfield Charter Township, Grand Traverse County
moratoriums.duration_description: 1 year with an automatic 6-month extension (so up to 18 months total), approved by the township board Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026. Board Chair Joe McManus said the deliberate pace and defensible drafting were partly a response to other Michigan moratoriums now being challenged or overturned in court.
moratoriums.summary: Garfield Township trustees approved a data center moratorium on August 25, 2026 running one year with an automatic six-month extension, to study impacts on local water and power resources before any project (including a small-scale proposal on Sybrandt Road) can proceed. Board Chair Joe McManus said the township worked with legal counsel to write an enforceable version, after other Michigan communities saw faster-moving moratoriums challenged in court.
moratoriums.source_title: 9&10 News — Garfield Township enacts data center moratorium to buy time for research on restrictions

resources.title: Michigan Advance — Garfield Township puts a 1-year ban on data centers, cryptocurrency mining

moratoriums.duration_description: 6 months from August 25, 2026. Does not apply to DataBank's proposed second data center, already under planning-board review.
moratoriums.summary: The Orangetown Town Board passed a six-month moratorium on new data center and battery energy storage system applications on Tuesday, August 25, 2026, after a public hearing, to give the town time to study the impacts of future projects. It does not apply to DataBank's plans for a second data center already before the planning board, which residents criticized.
moratoriums.source_title: WAMC — Hudson Valley residents dissatisfied with data center moratorium

resources.title: Town of Orangetown (official) — Establishing a Temporary Moratorium on Data Centers and Battery Energy Storage Systems
News 12 Westchester — Orangetown Board Approves Moratorium On New Data Center Applications

moratoriums.duration_description: 12 months (Resolution No. 26-R-97, effective immediately upon August 18, 2026 adoption); the council may shorten or extend it based on the planning commission's progress. The commission is to report recommendations within 6 months on utility demand, cooling, stormwater, transportation and residential separation. Existing data-center businesses are unaffected unless they cease operating 60+ days or let their license lapse.
moratoriums.summary: The Anniston City Council adopted Resolution No. 26-R-97 on August 18, 2026, directing the city to withhold permits, approvals and licenses for locating, developing, expanding or operating a data center within its jurisdiction for 12 months. Officials emphasized the pause is a planning measure, not opposition to data centers, meant to put clear standards in place before any proposal arrives.
moratoriums.source_title: WBRC — City of Anniston adopts resolution that establishes temporary moratorium on data centers within regulatory jurisdiction

moratoriums.duration_description: 12 calendar months from the Sept. 16, 2026 vote, superseding an earlier 8-month pause. The county's own Planning and Zoning Commission had recommended 18 months; the Board settled on 12 so it could move forward with drafting regulations rather than prolong the process.
moratoriums.summary: Gage County supervisors approved a 12-month moratorium on data center permits on September 16, 2026, superseding an earlier eight-month pause, to give the county time to develop data-center-specific rules. Supervisor Emily Haxby said the county currently has no regulations in place for data centers and needs them before accepting a permit; Supervisor Rex Adams favored the shorter, 12-month term to keep the rulemaking process moving.
moratoriums.source_title: KLKN TV — Gage County approves 12-month data center moratorium

resources.title: Beatrice Daily Sun — Gage County Board votes for 12-month data center moratorium

moratoriums.duration_description: 6 months (Resolution 2026-47), unanimously approved June 16, 2026 -- the maximum length Colorado law allows the county to impose at one time. Commissioner Veronica Medina said she may eventually bring a long-term ban to voters.
moratoriums.summary: The Archuleta County Board of County Commissioners unanimously approved Resolution 2026-47 on June 16, 2026, imposing a six-month moratorium during which the county will not accept applications or engage in pre-submittal activity for data center facilities. Commissioner Veronica Medina cited the county's limited water supply and infrastructure, noting Colorado law caps a single moratorium at six months.
moratoriums.source_title: The Pagosa Springs Sun — Moratorium on data centers approved by county board

moratoriums.duration_description: 6 months from July 13, 2026. The moratorium lapses after 60 days if the city does not hold a public hearing within that period, and the council may extend or cancel it early.
moratoriums.summary: The Marysville City Council unanimously passed a six-month moratorium on Monday, July 13, 2026, barring construction of buildings or facilities whose principal use is the management or transmission of digital data, while the city completes its water and sewer master plans and associated rate studies. Incidental servers inside a business with a different primary use are not covered.
moratoriums.source_title: The Daily Herald (heraldnet.com) — Marysville initiates 6-month moratorium on data centers

moratoriums.duration_description: Originally 90 days from Feb. 17, 2026; extended May 5, 2026 through December 31, 2026 (or an earlier board vote to end it, approve an extension, or adopt an impact-fee ordinance). A separate proposed zoning text amendment that would have banned data centers outright failed 4-3 on Sept. 1, 2026, but that vote did not affect the moratorium itself, which remains in force.
moratoriums.summary: The Bulloch County Board of Commissioners approved a 90-day moratorium on data center permitting on February 17, 2026 to research whether data centers should be prohibited or allowed (and under what standards) in unincorporated Bulloch County; commissioners extended it May 5, 2026 through the end of 2026. A follow-on proposal to ban data centers outright via zoning text amendment failed 4-3 on September 1, 2026, leaving the moratorium itself -- and the underlying by-right question -- unresolved.
moratoriums.source_title: Statesboro Herald — Commissioners extend both moratoriums, step toward outright ban on data centers

resources.title: WTOC — Bulloch County data center moratorium remains in place after commissioners deadlock on text amendment
Grice Connect — Bulloch County implements moratoriums on data centers and residential rezonings (Feb 17, 2026 meeting)

moratoriums.duration_description: N/A -- a proposal to pause data center applications was voted down before any duration took effect.
moratoriums.summary: Indiantown's village council voted 4-1 against a proposed pause on data center applications on September 1-2, 2026, after hours of public comment and a threatened lawsuit from an attorney for the Silver Fox 606 data center project. The council instead directed staff to obtain a new legal opinion and lawsuit-resistant language. Shortly after the vote, the council also voted to terminate the village manager; interim counsel is expected to bring a revised resolution back within a week or two.
moratoriums.source_title: WFLX — Indiantown council votes against pausing data center projects to seek additional legal opinion
moratoriums.failure_reason: The council voted 4-1 against the pause on Tuesday, Sept. 1, 2026, opting instead to seek a new legal opinion and 'lawsuit-proof' language after an attorney for the Silver Fox 606 data center project threatened to sue if the village paused data center projects.

moratoriums.duration_description: N/A -- a proposed 1-year moratorium was voted down before taking effect.
moratoriums.summary: The Salix City Council voted 3-2 on Aug. 20, 2026 against a one-year data center moratorium, capping months of debate over roughly 900 acres of farmland the town annexed in April for a potential data center. MidAmerican Energy initiated the project, and Google was identified in early August as the prospective customer. Woodbury County is challenging the annexation in court.
moratoriums.source_title: Iowa Public Radio — Northwest Iowa town votes against a data center moratorium
moratoriums.failure_reason: The Salix City Council voted 3-2 against a proposed one-year moratorium on Thursday night, Aug. 20, 2026. Council member Denise Burkhart said the city needed more information from Google, identified in early August as the prospective customer, before deciding.
